name: vscode-css-peek
description: Allow peeking to css ID and class strings as definitions from html files to respective CSS. Allows peek and goto definition.
author: Pranay Prakash <pranay.gp@gmail.com>

cssPeek.supportTags.description: Enable Peeking from HTML tags in addition to classnames and IDs. React components are ignored, but it's a good idea to disable this feature when using Angular

cssPeek.peekVariables.description: Include preprocessor variable definitions (e.g. SCSS `$foo`, LESS `@foo`) in peek results. Disable to hide variables from go-to and peek definition.

cssPeek.peekFromLanguages.description: A list of vscode language names where the extension should be used.

cssPeek.peekToExclude.description: A list of file globs that filters out peekable files

cssPeek.peekToLinkedOnly.description: When enabled, peek targets are restricted to stylesheets that are referenced from the current source file (e.g. via <link rel="stylesheet" href="..."> in HTML or `import './foo.css'` / `@import 'foo.css'` in JS/TS/SCSS). Useful in large monorepos to avoid matching unrelated stylesheets.

cssPeek.trace.server.description: Traces the communication between VSCode and the language server.

cssPeek.enableTelemetry.description: Send anonymous usage data and error reports to help improve CSS Peek. Set to false to opt out. The extension also honors VSCode's global `telemetry.telemetryLevel` setting, so disabling telemetry there will also disable it here.

virtualWorkspaces.description: The extension currently relies on the `fs` module but it should be easy to change this. Please make a PR to help.

scripts.postinstall: cd client && yarn && cd ../server && yarn && cd ../tests && yarn && cd ..
